newsitem.title: ITALY: Kinkel says Germany to meet EMU goals in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Kinkel says Germany to meet EMU goals in 1997.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said in an interview with an Italian magazine economic criteria for a single European currency must be strictly respected.

"The federal government is making every effort to guarantee that Germany satisfies the Maastricht parameters in 1997. And we will do it," Kinkel said in the interview with Panorama weekly magazine released ahead of publication on Friday.
Kinkel told Panorama: "The euro, as agreed at Maastricht, must be introduced on January 1 1999. If we do not take this opportunity now, maybe it will not represent itself again for decades."
"We cannot give up the euro because the economy of the European Union, after the single market, must swiftly have its second pillar -- economic and monetary union," he said.
He said Germany continued to be among the firm supporters of the principle that only states which respect the EMU criteria will enter the single currency.
"The parameters...must be respected rigorously. And that will not change," he added.
